exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Reflection of a Sine Curve Over the Horizontal Axis

question.text: What is the equation of the graph shown above?
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y=\sin x.$

  • Then, reflect it in the $x$-axis to give $y=-\sin x.$

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y=-\sin x.$

example.title: Identifying the Reflection of a Sine Curve Over the Horizontal Axis

question.text: What is the equation of the graph shown above?
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y=\sin x.\phantom{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

  • Then, reflect it in the $x$-axis to give $y=-\sin x.\phantom{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

  • Finally, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ to give $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}\sin x$

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}\sin x.$

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Reflection of a Cosine Curve Over the Horizontal Axis

question.text: What is the equation of the graph shown above?
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \cos{x}.$

  • Then, reflect it in the $x$-axis to give $y = -\cos{x}.$

  • Finally, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $2.25$ to give $y = -2.25\cos{x}.$

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y = -2.25\cos{x}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Reflection of a Sine or Cosine Curve Over the Vertical Axis

question.text: Which of the following equations could be used to describe the graph shown above?
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y=\cos x.$

  • Now, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $2.$

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y=2\cos x.$

Notice that, because the cosine function is even, it is symmetric about the $y$-axis, i.e.,

\[ 2\cos x = 2\cos (-x) \]

So the graph could also be viewed as $y=2\cos(-x).$

example.title: Identifying the Reflection of a Sine or Cosine Curve Over the Vertical Axis

question.text: Which of the following equations could be used to describe the graph shown above?
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \sin{x}.$

  • Then, reflect it across the $y$-axis.

  • Finally, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $\dfrac{3}{2}.$

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y = \dfrac{3}{2}\sin(-x).$

Notice that, because the sine function is odd, the $y$-axis reflection has the same effect as the $x$-axis reflection, i.e., \[ \dfrac{3}{2}\sin(-x) = -\dfrac{3}{2}\sin{x}. \]

So the graph could also be viewed as $y = -\dfrac{3}{2}\sin{x}.$ However, $y = -\dfrac{3}{2}\sin{x}$ is not among the given options.

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Reflection and Shifting of a Sine or Cosine Curve

question.text: Identify the equation that generated the graph above.
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \cos{x}.$

  • Then, reflect it in the $x$-axis to give $y = -\cos{x}.$

  • Finally, translate it by $\dfrac{5}{2}$ units up to give $y = -\cos{x} + \dfrac{5}{2}.$

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y = -\cos{x} + \dfrac{5}{2}.$

example.title: Identifying the Reflection and Shifting of a Sine or Cosine Curve

question.text: Identify the equation that generated the graph above.
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y=\cos x.$

  • Then, reflect it in the $x$-axis to give $y=-\cos x.$

  • Finally, translate it by $2$ units down to give $y=-\cos x-2$

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y=-\cos x-2.$
